# Computed body and derived preparation first histories

These are three separate informed studies, not blind benchmarks. They retain
original sources, actual diagnostics and reported executable identities. Every
quantum example allocates at most two physical qubits; no maximum-size quantum
case was generated or checked. Checking observations and numerical runs remain
distinct from independent exact equations and current implementation validation.

The computed-body archive preserves all 54 original files, including six first
projects, their complete streams, both observer scripts and the separately linked
`attempt-02` repairs. The first five checks mistakenly name a parameterized
quantum declaration `main`; their actual `invalid_entry` refusals precede the
intended body checks. The hidden-reference case instead reaches the common
ownership refusal. Its prediction and that earlier refusal remain intact.
The second observer changes only `pub unitary fn main(` to
`pub unitary fn subject(` in all six sources. All six still refuse: derived Z,
the unrelated wrapper, H and the false-scalar Meaning stop at the old expanded
Z/T profile; derived T reaches the returned-ancilla slot ownership restriction;
the hidden outer reference remains forbidden. These early failures do not
establish the predicted exact Z/T equations or a scalar Meaning comparison.
`repair-plan.json` binds the untouched first plan and each original source;
repairs never replace first bytes or predictions. No program was executed.

The separate derived-preparation archive retains 22 original files and six
reported check/run invocations. Reference reset and the zero-width empty owner
each check and run successfully; falsely labeling reset `Unitary` refuses in
both commands. Successful checks report 182 and 168 native decisions, zero
independent requests, an entry without a complete request and source preservation
not proved. Runs record the reference/zero distributions approximately
`(false,false): 1/2`, `(true,false): 1/2`, and the empty result with probability
one. These numerical observations are not all-input/reference or exact
instrument equations. The Python stdin driver was not saved. No driver,
prediction, complete source freeze or pre/post source window is reconstructed.
The capture explicitly records dirty-source observation and no build attestation.

The later canonical-length archive preserves seven original files, its saved
observer and one accepted check of 1,025 exactly expanded sealed T actions.
It is a two-qubit compatibility baseline above the separate function-equation
step cap, not a maximum-width experiment or a new normalization proof.
Its report contains 164 native decisions, zero independent requests, an entry
without a complete request and source preservation not proved. No program was
executed. This unchanged sealed-body observation does not establish support for
long bodies after ordinary derived-T expansion or larger source identities.

Archive order is computed first/linked repairs, separate preparation, then the
later canonical-length baseline. The first and repaired computed windows are
identical and contain 201 source hashes; the later canonical window contains 203.
Each saved observer records stable before/after source and executable windows.
The preparation capture has no such source window. All three observed dirty
HEAD `460f72e019885bd859686b6f4a8b265b40ab36fd`, CLI SHA-256
`d20fbb4505ed3c11997929b487404ea225395f993ea53bb30183361dcbda6ed9`
and kernel SHA-256
`54c9d60b80f67217abd95c8fe6ec1c06aa262e142d5e6db30f46a20cb90faf07`.
Stable executable identities are not a clean commit-to-binary build attestation.
Reported argv and streams do not independently authenticate their observer.

Three deterministic fixed-metadata USTAR/gzip archives retain 83 unchanged files
/ 203,874 expanded bytes: computed body 54 / 126,471; preparation 22 / 9,050;
canonical length 7 / 68,353. `packets.json` binds each member's original bytes,
SHA-256 and mode-0644 identity. The existing per-archive 80-member, 5 MiB expanded
and 2 MiB stored bounds remain unchanged. The fourteen prior general-static,
runtime-transform and derived-phase/QFT retention files remain byte-identical.

The passive reader never executes recorded commands, sources or observer code
and never extracts archive members. It checks complete inventories, first/repair
lineage, original sources, complete streams, actual refusal categories, native
report scopes, bounded distributions and the saved windows as inert data.
This history does not complete #369/#167, source/native/runtime or target/resource
preservation, QS/PR/quantitative RS/EXACT obligations, any Issue or a release.
